## Precision Root Cause Analysis Update

After deeper investigation, I can now explain EXACTLY why this happens and why it is subagent-specific.

### Root Cause: 3-Layer Chain

**1. OpenCode API returns 402 for explicit model specification**
When a subagent prompt is sent with an explicit model parameter (provider=opencode-go, model=deepseek-v4-flash), the API returns 402 "Insufficient balance". If no explicit model is passed, the API uses the agent's default model and the call succeeds. This was confirmed: subagent_type="general" (no explicit model) works with deepseek, while subagent_type="oracle" (explicit model from config) fails.

**2. OMO plugin disables fallback chain when config model is set**
When the user configures a model in oh-my-opencode.json (explicitCategoryModel is set), the fallback chain from CATEGORY_MODEL_REQUIREMENTS is replaced with undefined. This means if the configured model fails billing, there is NO automatic retry with alternative models from the hardcoded fallback chain.

**3. Config fallback models only contain the same failing model**
The config's fallback_models only included the same model that already failed. So the retry loop also fails.

### Why Only Certain Models

Testing all 12 opencode-go/ models:
- minimax-m2.5 / minimax-m2.7 (MiniMax upstream) -> works
- All other 10 models -> 402

This matches previous upstream depletion events:
- Apr 26: Moonshot AI (Kimi) - raw upstream error confirmed (#24462)
- Apr 26: ZhipuAI (GLM) - confirmed upstream depletion (#24492)
- May 14: DeepSeek (V4 Flash/Pro) - same pattern
- May 17: MiMo - same 402 (#28018)

### Workaround

Setting agent/category models to opencode-go/minimax-m2.5 with opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash as fallback makes everything work. Main session can still use deepseek-v4-flash directly.

Thanks for the detailed report. I do not think this is actionable in stock OpenCode as written.

What I checked:

- Current OpenAI Responses API docs explicitly show `gpt-5.5` accepting `max_output_tokens`.
- OpenCode built-in OpenAI/Codex plugin already clears `output.maxOutputTokens` for provider `openai` to match Codex CLI behavior, so stock OpenCode should not send `max_output_tokens` on that path. This is present in `v1.14.50` and current `dev`.
- We have a regression assertion for the OpenAI Responses payload that expects `max_output_tokens` to be absent, and that focused test passes locally.

Given the workaround says removing `@iam-brain/opencode-codex-auth` fixes it, this looks like the third-party plugin is either reintroducing the cap after OpenCode built-in hook or running a custom request path. If you can reproduce this with stock OpenCode, default plugins enabled, and no third-party Codex auth plugin, please reopen with the raw request body and startup flags/config.

> what are the use cases for this?

As I mentioned, regarding scenarios where the parent agent needs to supervise child agents:
First, concerning proactive supervision and early interruption: In certain cases, a child agent might not fully grasp the parent agent's instructions or requirements. In such instances, it is ideal for the parent agent to be able to proactively cancel these sub-tasks. This is also applicable when the parent agent is clearly unsatisfied with the child agent's output, or when the user explicitly requests the parent agent to oversee and guide the child agent until a high-quality deliverable is produced. This is especially true in document-writing scenarios, which often require ongoing mid-course corrections and prompting. For automated workflows where users prefer a hands-off approach, allowing the parent agent to periodically monitor the child agent after receiving the initial command is a much better alternative. Timely interruption and correction of the child agent's reasoning can also significantly save tokens.
Second, concerning asynchronous collaboration and pipelining: Certain workflows require two agents to collaborate—for example, one agent writing code and another writing documentation, where each document corresponds to a code chapter, and all subsequent docs/code depend on previous ones. Based on my experience with similar tasks, in the current implementation, once a child agent finishes, the parent agent collects the output, spins up the next child agent for the next chapter, and then resumes its own tasks. However, in reality, the two agents may operate at different speeds. A child agent might finish its next chapter much earlier, but because the parent agent only assigns one chapter at a time, it sits idle waiting for the parent agent to finish writing, review the progress, and assign the next task. Conversely, sometimes the parent agent finishes first and waits for the child agent, depending entirely on the workload of each chapter, which can vary drastically. 
This setup leads to wasted overhead in spinning up child agents repeatedly and idle waiting times on both sides. Efficiency could be significantly improved if this mutual waiting time were utilized. Furthermore, for some workflows, executing all tasks in a single pass feels much more natural. If the parent agent is allowed to fetch the child agent's task progress at any time, it could dispatch all tasks at once while concurrently monitoring them for accuracy and completeness. If the performance falls short, the parent agent can interrupt immediately and provide more detailed guidance. Meanwhile, the parent agent can fetch the child agent's latest results whenever it completes its own chunk of work, allowing the child agent to keep running and the parent agent to advance the overall workflow with the retrieved data. This would make the entire process much more fluid and natural.
